# Sparkline

A sparkline: a small trend line without axes, for stat tiles and table cells. It is purely graphic: there is
no hover, and the exact values belong next to it or in a table.

**Interaction**: not interactive. The line is 2 px with round joins; by default the history is in the
de-emphasis color and the last value is an accent dot. A gap in the data breaks the line; a lone value is drawn
as a dot. Screen readers read the label and a summary: first and last value, low and high.

**Category**: Charts · **Common uses**: Trends in stat tiles, a trend column in tables, activity over the last weeks in list items

## Import

```ts
import { Sparkline } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

By default the history is in the de-emphasis color and the latest value is an accent dot. The width fills the
container; `label` is what screen readers read, followed by a summary of the values. The dot has a ring in the
surface color, so place sparklines on a surface such as a Panel.

```tsx
export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Panel>
      <Stack gap={2}>
        <Text size="sm" tone="secondary">
          Visits, last 12 weeks
        </Text>
        <Sparkline data={visits} label="Visits in the last 12 weeks" area />
      </Stack>
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

## Variants

### Highlight and color

`highlight="none"` draws one plain line in the first chart color; `slot` draws the whole line in another chart
color, for a sparkline that stands for a series shown elsewhere in that color.

```tsx
export function Variants() {
  return (
    <Panel>
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <Sparkline data={visits} label="Visits, plain line" highlight="none" />
        <Sparkline data={visits} label="Visits, in the second chart color" slot={2} area />
        <Sparkline
          data={visits}
          label="Visits, in the second chart color without a dot"
          slot={2}
          highlight="none"
        />
      </Stack>
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

### In a table

`size="sm"` (20 px high) fits a table cell or a list item; give the column a width.

```tsx
export function InTable() {
  return (
    <Panel flush>
      <DataTable
        aria-label="Projects"
        rowKey={(row) => row.name}
        rows={[
          { name: 'Atlas', builds: [12, 14, 13, 17, 19, 18, 22, 24] },
          { name: 'Beacon', builds: [31, 29, 30, 26, 24, 25, 21, 19] },
          { name: 'Cobalt', builds: [8, 9, 8, 8, 9, 8, 9, 9] },
        ]}
        columns={[
          { key: 'name', title: 'Project' },
          {
            key: 'builds',
            title: 'Builds, last 8 weeks',
            width: 200,
            render: (row) => (
              <Sparkline
                data={row.builds}
                label={`${row.name}, builds in the last 8 weeks`}
                size="sm"
              />
            ),
          },
        ]}
      />
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

## States

### Gaps and short data

A `null` breaks the line, and a lone value between gaps is drawn as a small dot. A single value is a dot at
the end; no values draw nothing.

```tsx
export function Gaps() {
  return (
    <Panel>
      <Stack gap={5}>
        <Sparkline
          data={[40, 44, 41, null, null, 52, 55, null, 49, null, 58, 61]}
          label="Uptime checks with missing days"
        />
        <Sparkline data={[42]} label="First week" />
        <Sparkline data={[]} label="No data yet" />
      </Stack>
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `readonly (number \| null)[]` | The values, oldest first. `null` (and `NaN`) leaves a gap: the line breaks there. An empty list, or a list of `null` only, draws nothing. | — | Yes |
| `label` | `string` | What the line shows, such as "Visits in the last 12 weeks". Required: screen readers read it followed by a summary (first and last value, low and high). | — | Yes |
| `area` | `boolean` | Fills the area under the line with a wash of the line color (about 10% opacity). | — | No |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | Height: `sm` (20 px) in table cells, `md` (32 px) in stat tiles. The width always fills the container. | `'md'` | No |
| `highlight` | `'last' \| 'none'` | `last`: the history is drawn in the de-emphasis color and the last value is a dot in the accent color, so the current value stands out (the rule for stat tile trends). `none`: one plain line in the first chart color, without a dot. | `'last'` | No |
| `slot` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 7 \| 8` | Draws the whole line in this chart color (1–8), for a sparkline that stands for a series shown elsewhere in the same color. History and current value are then not told apart by color; with `highlight="last"` the last value still gets a dot of the same color. | — | No |
| `format` | `ValueFormat` | How the values are written in the summary read by screen readers. | `'auto'` | No |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
